title: Exponential moment bound for a sign sum
statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $a_i\in\mathbb R$ for $i\in\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ satisfy $\sum_i a_i^2=1$, and let $t\in\mathbb R$. For a uniform Boolean vector $X\in\{0,1\}^n$, the exponential moment satisfies
\[\mathbb E\exp\!\left(t\sum_i a_i\sigma(X_i)\right)\leq\exp(t^2/2),\]
where $\sigma$ is the sign encoding.
hypotheses_covered: The sum of squared coefficients equals $1$
replaced:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $(a_i)_{i<n}$ be real coefficients with $\sum_{i<n}a_i^2=1$.
For the linear form $L(x)=\sum_{i<n}a_i(-1)^{x_i}$ on $\{0,1\}^n$, with uniform expectation $\mathbb E[h]=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}h(x)$, every $t\in\mathbb R$ satisfies
\[
\mathbb E[e^{tL(x)}]\le e^{t^2/2}.
\]
